xray.body: On a panoramic radiograph, follow the mandibular body along its lower border to the angle and ascending ramus on each side. bullets: Contrast its laryngeal-cartilage attachment region with the upper constrictor’s pterygoid–mandibular region. The absent middle constrictor must not be inferred from the gap.
Do not use its lower edge as a patient-specific sphincter boundary, surgical landmark or complete muscle-layer map.

ct.body: Dedicated cine CT research labels levator veli palatini near the pharyngeal auditory tube. A separate cadaver dissection describes the muscle below, and approximately parallel to, the tube on its course toward the soft palate.
bullets: The CT study included ten participants and used tube-oriented dynamic acquisitions. Its illustrated structures are labelled on one side for clarity; this is not a bilateral segmentation accuracy study.

mri.title: Right levator veli palatini · MRI orientation · draft

bullets: Follow the paired muscle toward the velum across adjacent images; a single sagittal section does not show the complete sling.
Muscle length and orientation changed with the speech task. A resting anatomical image and a dynamic speech sequence answer different questions.
The research acquisition does not establish routine brain-MRI visibility, an individual normal measurement or a validated moving Atlas muscle.

pathology.body: An aneurysm near the internal carotid–posterior communicating junction can affect the third cranial nerve. New double vision, eyelid droop or pupil change can be important, but not every third-nerve palsy is aneurysmal and pupil sparing alone cannot exclude an aneurysm.

A nearby nerve surface is not evidence of compression or a measured safe distance.

mri.title: Check ligament of right medial rectus · MRI orientation · draft
mri.body: Orient along the medial rectus toward the medial orbital wall. Human histology shows fine connections from its thick sleeve to periosteum; these are anatomic support structures, not an MRI-validated separately visible target.
bullets: The medial check ligament is associated with medial rectus fascia, away from the lateral rectus support and from the apical common tendinous origin.

The Atlas mesh is an anatomic reference, not an acquired MRI or patient-to-Atlas registration. Small fascial structures may be lost to acquisition resolution and partial-volume averaging; absence on a slice is not evidence of absence in the orbit.

In four normal volunteers scanned at 1 T with a surface coil, a high-resolution MRI study reported check ligaments among the connective structures seen. Its abstract does not establish separate medial or lateral identification, routine-protocol visibility or diagnostic accuracy.

pathology.body: Double vision can have different causes, including problems affecting eye alignment and movement. A passive orbital check ligament is not an eye muscle or cranial nerve; its selection cannot distinguish restricted movement from muscle weakness or a nerve disorder.

function.title: Commissure of fornix of forebrain · function evidence & limits · draft
function.body: The precise human functional role of the forniceal commissure remains unresolved. Histology found delicate crossing fibres between the crura; 7 T tractography in 178 people found no crossing connection, and nine dissections found no macroscopic tract. A separate study associated reconstructed dorsal hippocampal commissure measures with recognition-memory performance, without establishing causation or the identity of this surface.
bullets: The histology does not prove a direct hippocampus-to-hippocampus memory route.

ct.title: Right common tendinous ring · CT orientation · draft
ct.body: The common tendinous-ring region is at the orbital apex, around the orbital opening of the optic canal and the central superior orbital fissure. The optic strut separates the canal from the fissure. Compare these landmarks with the assembled model for orientation. This is anatomical location teaching, not direct tendon depiction on CT; the selected tendon surface is not a contour identified on CT.
bullets: Source-bound static anatomy only. Restore assembled separation before comparing relationships; explode and isolate are model controls, not CT planes. No acquired-image annotation or patient registration is supplied.

Evidence of depiction is not a routine-visibility promise. Daniels et al. correlated coronal cadaver CT with sections and demonstrated apical annulus anatomy in selected clinical CT studies. The inspected abstract does not establish whether individual ring fibres or their precise boundaries are separable on a particular scan, nor a diagnostic sensitivity or protocol.

The detailed annular boundary is disputed. Naito et al. found a shared C-shaped origin for three recti with an independent superior rectus origin; Lacey et al. found a common tendinous origin. Ma et al. described posterior fibrous origins joining into a complete ring further anteriorly. These anatomical studies do not validate the topology, thickness or attachment footprint of this source mesh.

Keep the tendon region distinct from the optic nerve, rectus muscles and bony openings. Their proximity may help explain location but cannot substitute for direct tendon identification. Absence of a distinguishable ring on a slice does not prove anatomical absence; no pathology assessment or nerve-function inference is supplied.

ct.title: Left common tendinous ring · CT orientation · draft
ct.body: The common tendinous-ring region is at the orbital apex, around the orbital opening of the optic canal and the central superior orbital fissure. The optic strut separates the canal from the fissure. Compare these landmarks with the assembled model for orientation. This is anatomical location teaching, not direct tendon depiction on CT; the selected tendon surface is not a contour identified on CT.
bullets: Source-bound static anatomy only. Restore assembled separation before comparing relationships; explode and isolate are model controls, not CT planes. No acquired-image annotation or patient registration is supplied.

Evidence of depiction is not a routine-visibility promise. Daniels et al. correlated coronal cadaver CT with sections and demonstrated apical annulus anatomy in selected clinical CT studies. The inspected abstract does not establish whether individual ring fibres or their precise boundaries are separable on a particular scan, nor a diagnostic sensitivity or protocol.

The detailed annular boundary is disputed. Naito et al. found a shared C-shaped origin for three recti with an independent superior rectus origin; Lacey et al. found a common tendinous origin. Ma et al. described posterior fibrous origins joining into a complete ring further anteriorly. These anatomical studies do not validate the topology, thickness or attachment footprint of this source mesh.

Keep the tendon region distinct from the optic nerve, rectus muscles and bony openings. Their proximity may help explain location but cannot substitute for direct tendon identification. Absence of a distinguishable ring on a slice does not prove anatomical absence; no pathology assessment or nerve-function inference is supplied.
ct.note: Original educational source draft; revision-bound radiologist review and sign-off are pending. Source geometry remains unvalidated. Atlas, imaging-case and paid-lecture access remain independent.

mri.title: Left common tendinous ring · MRI orientation · draft
mri.body: Use the posterior convergence of the rectus muscles and optic-nerve corridor to orient to the common tendinous origin at the orbital apex. Cadaver studies disagree on the precise participation of the superior rectus, so this draft does not impose one complete ring boundary on MRI.
bullets: This apical origin is separate from the anterior trochlea and the more anterior rectus sleeves. Their proximity in a model does not show a continuous tendon on a scan.

The Atlas mesh is an anatomic reference, not an acquired MRI or patient-to-Atlas registration. Small fascial structures may be lost to acquisition resolution and partial-volume averaging; absence on a slice is not evidence of absence in the orbit.

No individual check-ligament MRI visibility or diagnostic performance is established here. The orbital-apex tendon has disputed detailed boundaries in cadaver studies; do not infer them from the mesh or a single MR slice.
mri.note: Revision-bound radiologist review pending. No scan, patient registration, diagnostic finding or clinical approval is supplied. Atlas, imaging-case and lecture access remain independent.

mri.title: Left upper second secondary molar tooth · MRI methods orientation · draft
mri.body: These eight source-labelled first and second molars span both arches and sides; third molars are outside this subset. bullets: In the cited 2025 left lower first-molar study, proton-density weighting performed best for the tested visibility measures under its protocol.

xray.title: Epiglottis · Lateral neck radiograph orientation · draft
xray.body: On a lateral neck radiograph, vallecular air can outline the anterior margin of the epiglottis, while laryngeal air can outline its posterior margin. pathology.title: Epiglottis · Injury & disease · draft
pathology.body: Epiglottitis causes swelling near the laryngeal entrance and can obstruct breathing. It is an emergency, not simply a label for any sore throat or an unusually shaped reference epiglottis.
bullets: Severe throat pain, painful swallowing, drooling and noisy or difficult breathing may occur.
A static open-looking model cannot establish that a person's airway is safe.

ultrasound.title: Right lacrimal canaliculus · Ultrasound acquisition and limits · draft
ultrasound.body: Specialist ultrasound biomicroscopy can depict portions of the upper lacrimal drainage apparatus. A 40–70 MHz in-vivo study of 22 eyes mapped proximal canaliculi; a separate 80 MHz study examined canaliculi in 40 normal eyes. These are acquisition-specific observations, not a promise that routine ultrasound depicts each canaliculus.
bullets: The 80 MHz study reported only 2 mm tissue penetration. A modified ultrasound biomicroscopy study of 24 normal drainage systems also described medial-canthal positioning and eye-cup difficulties. Depth and access constrain what can be shown.

The selected side has one canaliculus-labelled Atlas mesh. It does not resolve upper, lower or common canalicular subdivisions, demonstrate a lumen, or validate continuity with the sac or deeper duct.

bullets: A narrow-looking reference surface is not evidence of obstruction.

ultrasound.title: Right lacrimal sac · Ultrasound acquisition and limits · draft
ultrasound.body: The lacrimal sac can be approached in selected specialist ultrasound studies, but its image appearance depends on acquisition and physiological or disease state. In a 40–70 MHz study of 22 eyes, the sac lumen differed at rest, during irrigation, and with nasolacrimal obstruction. A separate direct-contact 10 MHz B-mode study compared sacs in ten adults with normal drainage and ten with chronic dacryocystitis.
bullets: A modified ultrasound biomicroscopy study assessed 24 normal drainage systems using an adapted setup; ordinary probe placement at the medial canthus was a stated obstacle. These small, different study groups do not define one general healthy appearance.
The selected sac-labelled Atlas surface is an unvalidated envelope. It does not identify an image cavity, contents, fluid, disease, tear flow, patency, or continuity through the full duct.
No acquired sac image, patient-space registration, mesh-to-image correspondence, diagnostic accuracy or congenital applicability is supplied.
ultrasound.note: Original educational draft for Didanix Education/light. No acquired image or patient-space registration is supplied. Revision-bound radiologist review is pending; Atlas, case and lecture access remain independent.

pathology.title: Right lacrimal sac · Injury & disease · draft
pathology.body: Dacryocystitis involves inflammation and infection of the lacrimal sac, commonly with impaired tear drainage. Painful swelling near the inner eye corner or discharge may occur.
bullets: Sac disease is distinct from lacrimal-gland inflammation and canaliculitis.
A reference sac does not show pus, abscess formation or the site of a blockage.
Two separately indexed sac surfaces, not a filling reservoir, validated lumen or infected cavity. The medial tear-drainage location must not be confused with the upper outer tear-producing gland.

mri.title: Tarsal plate of right upper eyelid · MRI orientation · draft
mri.body: At the upper eyelid, locate the tarsal plate within the lid rather than within the globe or orbital septum. A dedicated eyelid MRI study identified superior tarsal plates on T1- and T2-weighted images.
bullets: The upper plate belongs to the upper lid. The nearby orbital septum and levator complex are separate layers; a single low-resolution slice may blend them.

The Atlas mesh is an anatomic reference, not an acquired MRI or patient-to-Atlas registration. Small fascial structures may be lost to acquisition resolution and partial-volume averaging; absence on a slice is not evidence of absence in the orbit.

No individual check-ligament MRI visibility or diagnostic performance is established here. The orbital-apex tendon has disputed detailed boundaries in cadaver studies; do not infer them from the mesh or a single MR slice.

pathology.title: Tarsal plate of right upper eyelid · Injury & disease · draft
pathology.body: A chalazion arises from blockage of a meibomian gland in the eyelid. The tarsal plate provides anatomical context, but the plate is dense connective tissue, not the gland itself and not cartilage.

ultrasound.title: Right thyrohyoid membrane · Ultrasound membrane orientation · draft
ultrasound.body: Orient the thyrohyoid membrane between the hyoid bone and thyroid cartilage. Society teaching describes it as a bright connecting line. In a study of 40 healthy volunteers, investigators identified the membrane but did not visualize the internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve.
bullets: The right and left Atlas selections are source-model surfaces. The cited study does not validate their separate sonographic boundaries; use the selected side for orientation only.

Seeing the epiglottis through the thyrohyoid window is a different observation from identifying the membrane itself. Neither observation identifies every nearby nerve or validates the model against a scan.

pathology.title: Tentorium cerebelli (right-sided source only) · Tentorial involvement: attachment is not enhancement · draft

bullets: Assess the lesion itself and its relationship to the dural fold; do not infer tentorial involvement from an enhancing line or from apparent contact with this reference surface alone. The cited historical series does not establish a current universal diagnostic rule.

Learning check: do the reports prove that a normal inferior thyroid artery is visible on every neck MRI? No. They describe individual MRA examinations, without a normal-vessel detection study or a registered MRI-to-Atlas comparison.

ct.title: Left inferior thyroid artery · CTA: confirm the arterial origin · draft
ct.body: CT angiography can show where an inferior thyroid artery originates. In a 210-subject CTA study, origins from the thyrocervical trunk, subclavian artery and vertebral artery were observed. The mapped parent in a reference atlas is therefore not a substitute for tracing the actual vessel in a patient acquisition.
bullets: Orient using the selected side and its mapped thyrocervical parent, then check the vessel origin independently on source images. The study does not establish visibility of every terminal branch in every acquisition.

In a reported pseudoaneurysm, CT/CTA depicted a cervical haematoma and mass effect; angiography confirmed the inferior thyroid arterial feeder. A nearby arterial surface alone does not identify the source of bleeding.
Source limit: one source-labelled inferior thyroid artery, not complete glandular supply, a verified patent junction, a lumen or the recurrent laryngeal nerve. No lesion or scan has been added.

mri.title: Left inferior thyroid artery · Inferior thyroid artery: distinguish MRA cases from routine MRI · evidence pending
mri.body: Two case reports describe neck MR angiography identifying an abnormal inferior thyroid artery: a right-sided course through thyroid tissue in one report and left-sided aneurysms in the other. These selected cases do not establish routine visibility of a normal artery on structural neck MRI.
bullets: On an acquired neck MRA, check the actual acquisition and trace vessel identity, side and parent independently of the Atlas label. Neither report establishes normal-vessel detection rates or visibility across routine structural MRI sequences.

The right-sided variant and left-sided aneurysmal disease belong to separate published cases, not this generic model or the owner’s scans. Colour, calibre and position of this reference surface do not establish either finding.

Learning check: do the reports prove that a normal inferior thyroid artery is visible on every neck MRI? No. They describe individual MRA examinations, without a normal-vessel detection study or a registered MRI-to-Atlas comparison.

This source surface supplies no acquired scan, measured flow, patient registration, verified recurrent laryngeal nerve relationship or validated procedural corridor. Normal-vessel identification evidence remains needed for the intended MRI protocol.

pathology.title: Left stria medullaris of thalamus · pathology evidence & limits · draft
pathology.body: The habenular pathway is studied in relation to mood circuits, but the 2022 tractography cohort comprised healthy participants. Reported differences in reconstructed streamline counts by sex and handedness describe the method’s outputs; they are not axon counts or disease markers. The study did not test whether stria injury causes depression or whether stimulation of this tract treats it. A lesion near the habenula requires patient-specific evidence before attributing symptoms to these small fibres.
bullets: A reconstructed streamline or atlas surface is not a disease biomarker.
Do not transfer research streamline differences to an individual lesion or treatment prediction.

clinical.title: Left stria medullaris of thalamus · clinical evidence & limits · draft
clinical.body: The stria medullaris carries afferent fibres toward the habenular region along the dorsomedial thalamus. In a research series of 30 healthy participants, probabilistic diffusion tractography reconstructed the pathway using pallidal seed and ventral-tegmental target regions with a habenular waypoint. This demonstrates an imaging method, not reliable visibility on routine MRI, individual axonal continuity or a validated clinical target.
bullets: Left and right source selections share this teaching; neither is registered to a patient tractogram.
Keep the stria medullaris distinct from the amygdala-related stria terminalis.

function.title: Septum of telencephalon · function evidence & limits · draft
function.body: The source label “septum of telencephalon” covers a broad region. Human anatomy distinguishes the dorsal septum pellucidum from the basal septum verum containing septal nuclei, though their tissue boundary is not sharp. Connections to hippocampal circuitry are described anatomically; rhythm-regulation evidence largely comes from animal work, with precise human function unresolved.

clinical.title: Right middle cerebral artery · Right hemispheric clinical context · draft
clinical.body: The middle cerebral artery arises from the internal carotid artery and supplies much of the lateral frontal, parietal and temporal cortex. Right-hemisphere stroke can cause left-sided spatial neglect: reduced awareness of the left side is a clinical finding, not a property visible in this artery model. Symptoms alone do not prove which arterial branch is affected.

function.title: Short ciliary nerve · source group · Pupil and accommodation pathways · draft
function.body: Short ciliary nerves carry postganglionic parasympathetic fibres from the ciliary ganglion towards the eye. Their targets include sphincter pupillae, which constricts the pupil, and ciliary muscle, whose contraction reduces zonular tension during accommodation.
bullets: Preganglionic parasympathetic input reaches the ganglion through the oculomotor route and synapses there. Sensory and sympathetic fibres associated with the ganglion do not share that parasympathetic synapse.
Short ciliary nerves are not exclusively parasympathetic. Human dissection describes sensory and sympathetic fibres alongside the parasympathetic component.
Use the orbital study window to relate the source group to the ganglion and globe. Mesh colour, branches and contact points do not identify fibre type, synapses or an intact physiological circuit.

pathology.title: Short ciliary nerve · source group · Tonic pupil and postganglionic injury · draft
pathology.body: Damage to the postganglionic parasympathetic pathway can impair pupil constriction and accommodation. Adie tonic pupil provides a clinical example: the pupil may respond poorly to light, with segmental iris-sphincter weakness and increased sensitivity to cholinergic stimulation. These functional findings do not identify an injured branch in this source mesh.
bullets: A 1977 study found regional reduction of corneal sensation in 10 of 11 people with unilateral Adie tonic pupil. This supported a shared orbital pathway localisation, not proof of a lesion in a particular displayed nerve or a population prevalence estimate.

Yoo et al. (2021) retrospectively compared dilute-pilocarpine responses in 56 patients with unilateral Adie tonic pupil and 61 controls with other causes of a dilated pupil. Responses depend on the testing conditions; supersensitivity is not a standalone diagnosis or a reason to assume all anisocoria is benign.

Ebrahim et al. (2009) reported tonic pupil after retinal-detachment surgery using endolaser. Injury to short ciliary parasympathetic fibres was a proposed explanation in one case, not demonstrated nerve histology or an estimate of surgical risk.

Use the intact orbital view to connect these findings with the ganglion and globe. This bilateral source group does not depict a diseased side, individual fibre loss, iris movement, pupil responses or a patient-specific lesion. Clinical examination and appropriate investigation remain separate from atlas orientation.

clinical.title: Short ciliary nerve · source group · Orbital injury and localisation limits · draft
clinical.body: Disruption of this parasympathetic pathway may affect pupil and accommodation functions. This is pathway-level context: a dilated pupil does not identify damage to an individual branch displayed in this atlas.
bullets: A 20-orbit cadaveric study described variation in ganglion roots and proposed a possible anatomical explanation for postganglionic mydriasis after orbital-floor fracture or repair. It did not establish diagnostic accuracy or a universal injury mechanism.

Interpret the nerve group with its orbital neighbours, not as a standalone lesion map. The source model cannot establish which fibres are injured, whether function is preserved or which procedure is safe.
